findings.claim: The plan puts each batch under its own timeout but never says what KMCTL_AUDIT_TIMEOUT now means or how the batches together fit the step's timeout-minutes of 40. Today one 30m limit sits inside 40 minutes. With N batches each allowed 30m, three slow batches can run 90 minutes. GitHub then kills the step at 40 minutes with no message from the script, and since the step is all or nothing, every finding from the batches that finished is lost. That is the silent failure f2 was meant to remove. The plan has to pick the meaning: a total budget split across batches (a per-batch limit taken from the time left, ending with the script's own message before timeout-minutes is reached), or a per-batch limit plus a total cap. It must also say whether action.yml, the workflow comment and the how-to text ('stops Hermes after 30 minutes') change. No eval row covers it.

The plan says 'batches of at most ten' but not whether it keeps the audit skill's step 2, batch by kind. It changes the scope: grouped by kind, each prompt carries only its own review skill, and the prompt text stops saying 'audit the batches one after another'. If kinds are mixed, every prompt carries all the needed review skills. r1 (25 concepts, 3 runs) does not settle it: 10/10/5 of one kind passes either way, and by kind a mixed set of 25 can need 4 or more runs. The plan should state the rule (keeping by kind matches the skill) and r1 should name the fixture's kinds and the expected runs per kind.

The plan now makes KMCTL_AUDIT_TIMEOUT one total budget: each batch's timeout gets the time left, and when it runs out the step fails naming the unfinished batches, inside the step's timeout-minutes of 40. It says which docs stay true and which line the how-to adds. Row r5 covers it.
The plan now groups batches by kind, gives each prompt only that kind's review skill, and r1 pins a 12/8/5 fixture expecting 4 runs (2, 1, 1 per kind).

add re-serialises each batch's findings with json.dumps, which writes a string the model escaped as \u0060\u0060\u0060 as a literal ``` fence. The merged file then no longer parses: the next batch's add fails and the error blames that batch, and when it was the last batch audit-report.py fails. Before this change, audit-report.py read the reply itself and accepted the same reply.
